Assert that a set of violations is empty

Source: R/ensure_empty.R
ensure_empty.Rd

The most general checkpoint. Express a rule as "the set of violations must be empty", build that set with an ordinary dplyr::filter() or an anti-join, and pipe it in. A rule that dplyr can express is a rule ensure_empty() can check, also one no other checkpoint covers:

Usage

ensure_empty(data, success_msg = NULL, warn_msg = NULL, abort_msg = NULL)

Arguments

data

The violation set: a data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables in checkpoints.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when data has rows and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to "The dataset is not empty.".

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

income |>
  dplyr::anti_join(population, by = "cpr") |>
  ensure_empty(abort_msg = "Income for persons outside the population")

When the data has no rows, a success line is printed. Otherwise ensure_empty() warns, or aborts with abort_msg, and shows the number of rows and the first few of them. Wrap the check in violations() to get all of them.

Unlike the other checkpoints, ensure_empty() returns the violation set it was given, not the data the rule is about, so it usually ends a pipeline. Use ensure_none() or ensure_all() to check a condition and carry on with all rows.

See also

ensure_none() and ensure_all() to check a condition without leaving the pipeline, tally_violations() to count many rules at once, violations() for all rows of a failed check, checkpoints.

Examples

# Success: no rows
ensure_empty(data.frame())
#> ✔ The dataset is empty.

# Warning: unexpected rows
mtcars |>
  dplyr::filter(cyl > 6) |>
  ensure_empty(warn_msg = "Eight-cylinder cars found")
#> Warning: Eight-cylinder cars found
#> ℹ 14 rows found:
#>       mpg   cyl  disp    hp  drat    wt  qsec    vs    am  gear  carb
#>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>   1  18.7     8  360    175  3.15  3.44  17.0     0     0     3     2
#>   2  14.3     8  360    245  3.21  3.57  15.8     0     0     3     4
#>   3  16.4     8  276.   180  3.07  4.07  17.4     0     0     3     3
#>   4  17.3     8  276.   180  3.07  3.73  17.6     0     0     3     3
#>   5  15.2     8  276.   180  3.07  3.78  18       0     0     3     3
#>   # ℹ 9 more rows
#> ℹ Wrap the check in violations() to get all rows.

# Many rules at once, then one judgement
mtcars |>
  tally_violations(
    "Few cylinders" = cyl < 4,
    "High mileage"  = mpg > 30
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(n > 0) |>
  ensure_empty(warn_msg = "Rules with violations")
#> Warning: Rules with violations
#> ℹ 1 row found:
#>     rule             n total rows
#>     <chr>        <int> <int> <list>
#>   1 High mileage     4    32 <int [4]>

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Abort: treat unexpected rows as a hard error
dplyr::starwars |>
  dplyr::filter(height < 0) |>
  ensure_empty(abort_msg = "Impossible: negative height")
} # }
